blocks.text: The chapter’s sequence is important: the returned community rebuilds the altar and resumes offerings before the temple itself is complete. Only afterward do they lay the temple foundation. The celebration at that moment is therefore not a simple, uniform triumph: praise and shouting mingle with loud weeping from older people who had seen the first house.

The weeping in verses 12–13 has been read alongside Haggai 2, which addresses people who remembered the house in its former glory and acknowledges that the present work could seem insignificant by comparison. A related question remains disputed: Haggai’s reference to the day the temple was founded may refer to later work, to earlier foundation traditions, or to a rhetorical way of marking a new beginning. The passage preserves the emotional force of comparison without resolving that question.

sections.title: A Question Raised by the Mixed Response
